overview: From 2026-10-03 to 2026-10-04, ethereum-optimism/optimism had 4 new PRs (0 merged), 4 new issues, and 13 active contributors.

topIssues.title: JWT secret generation should be consistent across the docs and not world-readable
topIssues.author: matthewdarwin
topIssues.body:
The docs generate the Engine API JWT secret in several places, and only one sets restrictive permissions.

With `chmod 600`:
- https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/c8e4ba855d79ca56463909ef5a2c5830a1189401/docs/public-docs/chain-operators/tutorials/create-l2-rollup/op-reth-setup.mdx#L59-L60 (and L314-L315)

Without it (world-readable under a typical umask):
- https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/c8e4ba855d79ca56463909ef5a2c5830a1189401/docs/public-docs/node-operators/tutorials/node-from-docker.mdx#L51
- https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/c8e4ba855d79ca56463909ef5a2c5830a1189401/docs/public-docs/node-operators/tutorials/run-node-from-source.mdx#L112
- https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/c8e4ba855d79ca56463909ef5a2c5830a1189401/docs/public-docs/node-operators/guides/configuration/execution-clients.mdx#L117
- https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/c8e4ba855d79ca56463909ef5a2c5830a1189401/docs/public-docs/node-operators/guides/configuration/consensus-clients.mdx#L106
- https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/c8e4ba855d79ca56463909ef5a2c5830a1189401/docs/public-docs/node-operators/guides/configuration/supernode-setup.mdx#L79
- https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/c8e4ba855d79ca56463909ef5a2c5830a1189401/docs/public-docs/chain-operators/guides/management/operations.mdx#L180

The examples should be consistent and secure by default, so the secret is readable only by the accounts that run the clients.

Related: op-reth's own auto-generated secret is also world-readable, because it comes from alloy's `JwtSecret::try_create_random`. That's raised upstream in alloy-rs/alloy#4291. geth writes its generated secret as `0600`, and Lighthouse is making the same change (sigp/lighthouse#10196).

topIssues.title: `eth_sendRawTransaction` troubleshooting should only point at the execution client's sequencer setting
topIssues.author: matthewdarwin
topIssues.body:
Step 2 of the `eth_sendRawTransaction` Does Not Exist solution says to inspect "every component that talks to the sequencer (`op-node`, `op-reth`, `op-batcher`, `op-proposer`, scripts)" for `--rollup.sequencer`:
https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/c8e4ba855d79ca56463909ef5a2c5830a1189401/docs/public-docs/node-operators/guides/troubleshooting.mdx#L91

Only the execution client forwards `eth_sendRawTransaction` to the sequencer, and `--rollup.sequencer` is an op-reth flag. op-node, op-batcher and op-proposer don't have it, so the list sends operators looking in places the setting can't be.

"Environment variables" would also be clearer as the service's own environment (unit `Environment=` / `EnvironmentFile=`, or container env) rather than the operator's shell.

topIssues.title: Create-L2-rollup examples should not expose the Engine API (8551) beyond op-node
topIssues.author: matthewdarwin
topIssues.body:
The create-L2-rollup example and tutorial bind op-reth's Engine API to all interfaces and publish it on the host:

- https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/c8e4ba855d79ca56463909ef5a2c5830a1189401/docs/public-docs/create-l2-rollup-example/docker-compose.yml#L56 (`"8551:8551"`, with `--authrpc.addr=0.0.0.0` at L73)
- https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/c8e4ba855d79ca56463909ef5a2c5830a1189401/docs/public-docs/chain-operators/tutorials/create-l2-rollup/op-reth-setup.mdx#L101 (same pattern, L116)
- https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/c8e4ba855d79ca56463909ef5a2c5830a1189401/docs/public-docs/chain-operators/tutorials/create-l2-rollup/op-reth-setup.mdx#L409 (bare-metal sequencer script, `--authrpc.addr=0.0.0.0` on the host)

op-node is the only consumer, and it already reaches op-reth over the Compose network (`--l2=http://op-reth:8551`), so the published port adds exposure without serving any purpose. Docker-published ports also bypass host firewalls such as ufw.

The Engine API authentication spec lists "RPC port exposed towards the internet" as a threat it guards against:
https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/blob/main/src/engine/authentication.md

The node-operator Docker tutorial already handles this correctly. It doesn't publish 8551 and connects via the container network:
https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/c8e4ba855d79ca56463909ef5a2c5830a1189401/docs/public-docs/node-operators/tutorials/node-from-docker.mdx#L133

Tutorial examples tend to be copied into production, so the chain-operator examples should match the node-operator one.

topIssues.title: Node troubleshooting: the op-reth `stage unwind` example should put `--datadir` and `--chain` before `to-block`
topIssues.author: matthewdarwin
topIssues.body:
The "Unclean Shutdowns → For op-reth" section gives:
https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/c8e4ba855d79ca56463909ef5a2c5830a1189401/docs/public-docs/node-operators/guides/troubleshooting.mdx#L110

```
op-reth stage unwind to-block <BLOCK_NUMBER> --datadir=<path>
```

According to the generated CLI reference in the same docs, `--datadir` is an option of `op-reth stage unwind`, not of the `to-block` subcommand, so it can't follow `to-block <BLOCK_NUMBER>`:
https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/c8e4ba855d79ca56463909ef5a2c5830a1189401/docs/public-docs/node-operators/op-reth/cli/op-reth/stage/unwind.mdx

The example also leaves out `--chain`, which defaults to `optimism` (OP Mainnet). An operator on any other chain who copies it would unwind with the wrong chain spec.

topPRs.title: cannon: bound preimage oracle requests
topPRs.author: obiyang
topPRs.body:
## Summary
Bound Cannon preimage requests and hint acknowledgements with a configurable `--oracle-timeout` (10 minutes by default).

## Problem
The existing 15-second polling interval only detects host exit. A live host that logs a failed request without responding can stall VM execution indefinitely.

## Solution
Give each request one deadline across all protocol phases, and cap file polling at that deadline. Recover timeout errors when the host has no process exit state yet, so the VM returns an error instead of panicking during recovery. Successful preimage bytes and the wire protocol are unchanged; operators can increase the timeout for slower hosts.

## Testing
- `go test -race ./cannon/cmd ./op-preimage` passed.
- `just go_test './cmd/... ./mipsevm/exec/... ./mipsevm/versions/...'` in `cannon` passed.
- `go test ./op-challenger/kvstore ./op-challenger/game/fault/preimages ./op-challenger/game/fault/trace/utils ./op-challenger/game/fault/trace/alphabet ./op-challenger/game/fault/trace/vm` passed.
- `just lint-go` passed with zero issues and clean module tidiness.
- CLI smoke run with the supported version-8 state and `--stop-at '=0'` passed. Regression tests fail when the request timeout, file deadline cap, or nil-state guard is removed.

## Related Issue
Fixes #15395

topPRs.title: op-node: expose automatic peer ban observability
topPRs.author: obiyang
topPRs.body:
## Summary
Add observability for automatic temporary peer bans.

## Problem
Automatic low-score peer bans have no corresponding metric, and disconnect logs lack the score context that triggered the ban.

## Solution
- Add an unlabeled `peer_bans` counter in the existing P2P namespace. It counts temporary ban registrations, including renewals, rather than distinct or currently banned peers.
- Record after expiry persistence succeeds and before disconnecting. A disconnect failure still counts the registered ban; persistence failures and zero-expiry clears do not count.
- Emit one structured debug log per completed low-score ban with peer, observed score, threshold, and expiry. Existing scoring, ban, disconnect, and unban behavior is preserved.

## Testing
All commands run from the repository root:
- `mise exec go@1.26.5 -- go test ./op-node/metrics ./op-node/p2p ./op-node/p2p/monitor ./op-node/p2p/gating -run 'TestRecordPeerBan|TestNodeP2PBanPeerMetrics|TestCheckNextPeer|TestExpiryConnectionGater' -count=1` — passed.
- `mise exec go@1.26.5 -- go test -race ./op-node/p2p/... ./op-node/metrics -count=1` — passed.
- `mise exec go@1.26.5 -- go test ./op-node/... ./op-supernode/supernode/chain_container/virtual_node ./op-e2e/e2eutils/opnode` — passed.
- `mise exec go@1.26.5 just@1.46.0 golangci-lint@2.8.0 -- just lint-go` — zero issues and clean module tidiness.
- Regression mutations confirmed the tests fail if counting occurs before persistence, after disconnect, or on zero-expiry clears. Restored sources and repeated the focused checks successfully.

Independent Go review found no outstanding concerns. Full repository and end-to-end suites were not run locally.

## Related Issue
Related to #15907. Broader score attribution, disconnect diagnostics, and gating-reason observability remain outside this contribution.

topPRs.title: op-node: expose SuperAuthority finalized head metrics
topPRs.author: obiyang
topPRs.body:
## Summary
Expose accepted SuperAuthority finalized L2 progress through the existing per-chain reference metrics.

## Problem
`l2_finalized` tracks local finality; materializing a SuperAuthority finalized reference updates a separate cache without publishing its progress.

## Solution
Record the distinct `l2_super_authority_finalized` type when an anchor or verified reference is accepted into that cache. Failed resolutions and rejected regressions retain the last metric values. Local finalized state and its metrics remain independent.

## Testing
- `cd op-node && mise exec go@1.26.5 just@1.46.0 gotestsum@1.12.3 -- just test` — passed.
- `mise exec go@1.26.5 -- go test -race ./op-node/rollup/engine/... ./op-node/metrics/...` — passed.
- `mise exec go@1.26.5 just@1.46.0 golangci-lint@2.8.0 -- just lint-go` — passed (0 issues; no module diff).
- The new exposition regression test fails without the metric emission and passes with it; it covers advancement, anchor resolution, failure retention, local-state independence, and per-chain labels.

## Related Issue
Fixes #20880

topPRs.title: op-conductor: avoid blocking WebSocket registration during shutdown
topPRs.author: zloglevel
topPRs.body:
**Description**

Prevent WebSocket handlers from blocking indefinitely when a connection is accepted while the op-conductor WebSocket hub is shutting down.

The hub uses an unbuffered registration channel. During shutdown, the hub may stop before the HTTP server finishes accepting requests. A newly upgraded WebSocket request could then block forever while sending the client to the registration channel.

This change makes WebSocket registration observe:

- Successful hub registration
- Hub shutdown
- Request context cancellation

When registration is rejected during shutdown or cancellation, the upgraded WebSocket connection is closed immediately.

**Tests**

Added `TestWebSocketRegistrationAfterHubShutdown`, which:

- Stops the WebSocket hub while keeping the HTTP listener active.
- Establishes a new WebSocket connection.
- Verifies that the handler does not remain blocked.
- Verifies that the connection is closed.
- Verifies that the client is not registered with the stopped hub.

Tests run:

```text
go test ./op-conductor/rpc/ws
go test -race ./op-conductor/rpc/ws -run 'TestWebSocketRegistrationAfterHubShutdown|TestHubShutdown' -count=1
```

**Additional context**

The existing shutdown ordering is preserved because `HTTPServer.Stop()` may wait for active WebSocket handlers. Closing the hub first allows existing clients and handlers to exit.

Changing the shutdown order alone would not eliminate the concurrent registration race, so registration now explicitly selects on the hub shutdown signal and request context.

**Metadata**

- Fixes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/22472

topPRs.title: docs: add Pinax to OP Stack RPC provider directory
topPRs.author: chillsauce
topPRs.body:
## Description

Adds **Pinax** to the Production RPC providers section of the OP Stack RPC directory.

Pinax is an infrastructure provider operating its own nodes for OP Stack networks, offering RPC alongside Firehose, Substreams, and the Token API. The entry follows the existing format on this page and is inserted alphabetically between OnFinality and PublicNode.

Coverage below is taken from our published per-chain support pages at [pinax.network/chain](https://pinax.network/) and verified live against our gateway before opening this PR:

| Network | Mainnet | Testnet | Token API |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| OP | ✅ OP Mainnet | ✅ OP Sepolia | ✅ |
| Unichain | ✅ Unichain | ✅ Unichain Sepolia | ✅ |
| Base | ✅ Base | ✅ Base Sepolia | ✅ |
| Ink | ✅ Ink | — | — |
| Soneium | ✅ Soneium | ✅ Soneium Minato | — |
| Zora | ✅ Zora | — | — |

RPC, Firehose, and Substreams are available on all six; the Token API is scoped to the three networks where it is actually offered.

## Tests

Content-only change to a single `.mdx` file. No build or behaviour changes; the added block reuses the exact structure of the surrounding provider entries. All links in the entry return HTTP 200.

## Additional context

Pinax (https://pinax.network/) has been providing blockchain data infrastructure since 2021, and is a core developer of Substreams and Firehose alongside StreamingFast.

## Metadata

- Docs-only change under `docs/public-docs/`.
